title: The rule of 72: how fast money doubles
examples: How long does money take to double?
How fast does a debt grow?

explain.say: Here's a magic trick for money: you can work out how long it takes to double, in your head! It's called the rule of 72. Look at the curve on the board. It shows savings growing with interest, the extra money a bank pays you for keeping your money there.

draw.text: The rule of 72: how fast money doubles

explain.say: The trick: divide 72 by the interest rate. If the bank pays 6 percent a year, 72 divided by 6 is 12. So your money doubles in about 12 years! See the first mark? 100 has become 200. What if the rate were 8 percent?

Yes, 72 divided by 8 is 9 years! Now look at the curve getting steeper. That's compound interest: you earn interest on your interest too. After 24 years at 6 percent, see the second mark, the money has doubled twice, to 400.

It works for loans too, in a less happy way. If you borrow at 18 percent and pay nothing back, 72 divided by 18 is 4, so the debt doubles in about 4 years! Which would you rather see doubling, savings or debt?

Look at the bars: 100, then 200, 400 and 800, doubling every 12 years. Well done! The rule is an estimate, but it's very close for rates between about 2 and 15 percent. Challenge: how long would money take to double at 3 percent?

faq.a: A quick way to estimate how many years money takes to double: divide 72 by the yearly interest rate. At 6 percent, it takes about 12 years.
asks: How do I work out how long money takes to double?

faq.a: Interest that is added to your money, so next year you earn interest on the interest too. It makes savings, and debts, grow faster and faster.
asks: Why does interest grow faster over time?

faq.q: Does the rule of 72 work for loans?
faq.a: Yes. It tells you roughly how fast an unpaid debt doubles. At 18 percent interest, it doubles in about 4 years.
asks: How fast does a debt double?

faq.q: How accurate is the rule of 72?
faq.a: It's an estimate, very close for interest rates between about 2 and 15 percent. At 6 percent, money really doubles in about 11.9 years.
72 divides neatly by many numbers, like 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12, and gives answers close to the exact maths. Some people use 70 or 69, which work slightly better at low rates.

facts: At 6% compound interest a year, money doubles in about 11.9 years.
The rule of 72 appears in Luca Pacioli's mathematics book of 1494.
